summary: Updates BCP 101 to account for the new IETF Intellectual Property Trust. It is a Best Current Practice and updates RFC 4071. It was replaced by RFC 8714.

plainLanguage.summary: The club set up a new box to hold its important ideas and logos. This updates the rule book to mention it.

subtitle: A short update to BCP 101 saying the new IETF Trust, not the Internet Society, owns and licenses IETF intellectual property.

tldr.problem: BCP 101 (RFC 4071) assumed the Internet Society would hold certain IETF-related intellectual property, but an IETF Trust had since been created for that purpose.
tldr.mechanism: The document says that references to ISOC in sections 3.1, 5.3 and 7 of RFC 4071 are to be read as the IETF Trust wherever IPR issues are concerned, and adds the Trustee duty to section 3.2.
tldr.outcome: It is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 4071 and was itself replaced by RFC 8714.

today: This Best Current Practice updates RFC 4071 and has been replaced by RFC 8714.

sections.title: Why BCP 101 Needed an Update
sections.content:
The first version of BCP 101, RFC 4071, assumed that the vehicle for certain IETF-related intellectual property rights (IPR) would be the Internet Society (ISOC). Since then, an IETF Trust has been created to hold such IPR, and this document updates RFC 4071 to match.

The update comes into force as soon as the IESG approves it and the IETF Trust Agreement has been formally signed by its Settlors and initial Trustees. Terms and abbreviations are as defined in RFC 4071.
sections.plainLanguage: The rule book named one keeper for the club's treasure. A new keeper was chosen, so the rule book needs a correction.

sections.title: What the Update Changes
sections.content:
The Trust was formed to acquire, hold, maintain and license certain existing and future intellectual property and other property used in the administration of the IETF. Its Settlors, who contributed initial intellectual property, were ISOC and the Corporation for National Research Initiatives. The Trustees are the members of the IAOC, and the Beneficiary is the IETF as a whole.

In administering IPR under BCP 101, the IASA, including the IAD and the IAOC, will treat the IETF Trust rather than ISOC as the proper entity for ownership and licensing of IETF IPR. References to ISOC in sections 3.1, 5.3 and 7 of RFC 4071 are interpreted as the IETF Trust wherever IPR issues are concerned, and the duty to serve as Trustees is added to section 3.2.
sections.plainLanguage: Wherever the old rule said the first keeper holds the treasure, read it as the new keeper. The people who run the club also become the new keeper's guardians.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document states that it has no security implications for the Internet. It changes which entity holds and licenses IETF intellectual property, not any protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: This is a paperwork change, so it does not make anything on the internet more or less safe.
